unit_tests.result: u_target, oracle_idx, losses and picks BIT-EXACT (torch.equal) vs reference for BOTH tf and onpolicy prefix policies. Call-count instrumentation confirms caching reduces individual_utility calls from K=4 (reference) to 1 (optimized_cache) inside one run_sequence call -- direct proof of the caching claim, not just an output-equivalence check.

scorer_coverage: cosine only, per the Phase-5 requested cell list (Individual/On-policy/Cosine). Asymmetric scorer not separately re-verified for A in OPT04 -- A caching is scorer-independent by construction (it only changes how many times individual_utility(futures, query_future) is called, never touches u_hat/arm_score/the metric), so this is a structural argument, not an empirical gap; flagged under NOT EXECUTED for completeness.
verdict: PASS -- caching (the OPT04-mandated approach, NOT the OPT03 norm-expansion algebra) is bit-exact at every level tested: isolated function calls, full run_sequence dispatch, and a real 10-optimizer-step training trajectory, for both tf and onpolicy.
